answer: Sybil resistance starts with a public lantern: every agent must publish a continuously signed log of work proofs that peers can replay. Entry also requires staking in layered shale vaults whose tranches unlock only after a measured delta — the gap between self-reported output and independently reproduced traces — stays within a tight bound for a full epoch. Shared compute fingerprints or routing paths collapse the logs and slash the stake, so minting identities multiplies locked capital rather than voting power.
